title: Set up your wallet
description: Create a wallet and go straight to receiving and sending. Winnow starts encrypted iCloud backup automatically when available.
journey: Create a wallet without a recovery-word checklist.
Reach the wallet home screen and see its backup status.
limitations: Without iCloud the wallet still works and shows Not backed up. Save a backup file; the recovery phrase and the backup controls are under Settings → Backup. The recorded simulator journey does not validate live iCloud.

title: Receive bitcoin
description: Receive shows an address at once. Label this address adds a local note saying who the address is for, or what the payment is for. Matching payments carry the note in your wallet.
journey: Tap Receive and read the address. A label is optional.
Return to the wallet; fund the address from the test node.
Check the funded balance and the received payment in Activity.
limitations: An address label does not verify the sender or create a payment destination. Labels are included in encrypted iCloud recovery, but not in manual wallet files.

title: An address and a card for one person
description: On Receive, under From one person, type a payer’s name. Winnow makes an ordinary address for them, for any wallet or an exchange, and a card for a payer who uses Winnow. The card holds a code made for them and neither of the wallet’s keys. Each payment made with it goes to an address of its own, and Activity names it as received from them.
journey: Open Receive. Under From one person, type the payer’s name and make their address and card.
The payer saves the card in Winnow and pays it to a fresh address, and also pays the ordinary address.
Activity names both payments as received from that person; their ordinary address advances after payment, and spending coins received through the card confirms.
limitations: Give the address and the card only to that person: anyone who has them can see what is paid with them. A wallet that holds only its account key cannot make a card.

title: Restore a post-backup card from iCloud
description: Payment cards derive from the wallet’s seed. Restoring an iCloud backup saved before a card existed still discovers payments sent to that card and lets you spend them.
journey: Back up a wallet to iCloud, then create a card for one person and receive a payment through it.
Restore the pre-card backup from iCloud on a fresh device.
Winnow discovers the post-backup card payment and spends the restored coin.
limitations: The recorded journey uses a simulated iCloud store rather than live Apple CloudKit.

screenshots.76-card-restore-icloud: Restoring a pre-card backup from iCloud
screenshots.77-card-restore-found: Post-backup card payment discovered on restore
screenshots.78-card-restore-spent: Spending the restored card coin confirms

title: Send bitcoin
description: Choose an account, recipient, and amount. Check the address, fee, and total before sending, or before collecting the account’s other signatures. A silent payment code works as a recipient too.
journey: Open Send, paste an address, and enter the amount.
Review the destination, amount, and fee before sending.
Check that Bitcoin Core accepts the payment; mine a block, see the receipt confirm, and return to wallet history.

title: Pay someone again
description: Name someone you’ve paid, or save their payment card. Next time, choose them in Send.
journey: Open a sent payment and save its recipient with a name.
Next time, choose the saved person in Send. A payment card can provide a fresh address for each payment.

title: Name who paid you
description: Give a received payment a local name without attaching an address. Add a payment card or explicitly choose a destination before sending.
journey: Open a received payment and save a local name for its sender.
Add a payment card or choose a destination explicitly before using Send to that person.
limitations: Funding addresses are unverified destinations, not proof of who paid you. Winnow never selects one automatically. Sending to an address again can reveal address reuse.

title: Choose a funding destination
description: If you choose to consult an explorer, review what is disclosed before asking. Then explicitly select any returned destination.
journey: Open the funding-address lookup and review the transaction ID and what the explorer learns before giving consent.
Choose a returned address explicitly, even if the explorer returns only one.
Save the destination with its unverified origin visible.
limitations: The explorer receives the transaction ID and your connection's IP address. Returned addresses do not identify people.

title: Share a wallet with other signers
description: Choose who signs and how many must sign. With two of three, one signer can be away and the other two can still pay. An optional recovery path lets fewer signers, or a recovery key, spend a coin that has not moved for a chosen number of blocks.
journey: Under Settings → Security → Multisig accounts, create a script-path 2-of-3 account from the phone’s key and two Bitcoin Core wallets’ keys, and receive test bitcoin into it.
Start the payment from Send with the account under From, and sign on the phone. Each Core wallet signs its copy of the PSBT and the phone combines them.
Send and check that the node accepts a transaction carrying exactly two signatures and that the app sees it confirm; after the recovery delay, spend with the recovery path.
limitations: Each signer keeps their own key. If you choose one required signature, any one of them can spend. Recovery words restore the wallet, not the account: keep the backup file or the iCloud copy.

screenshots.14-multisig-recovered: After the delay, the recovery path spends

title: Add a Ledger as a second key
description: Pair a Ledger under Settings → Security → Hardware wallets and keys and make a 2-of-2 with your phone. The Ledger shows the address and the payment on its own screen before it signs. With Bluetooth allowed, a Ledger in range while Winnow is open brings a card whose Set up pairs it, creates the 2-of-2 and has you compare the first address on both screens.
journey: Pair a Ledger over Bluetooth and create a 2-of-2 account from the phone’s key and the Ledger’s.
Check the receive address on the Ledger, fund the account, and review a payment.
Sign on the phone and on the Ledger; send and see the payment confirm in the account’s history.
limitations: The CI journey uses a simulated Ledger. A real Nano X co-signed a mainnet 2-of-2 with the earlier Swift app on 26 October 2026. Needs the Ledger Bitcoin app 2.1.2 or later (2.2.1 for a recovery path). Both keys are required: keep the wallet’s backup and the Ledger’s recovery words.

screenshots.25-ledger-nearby: A Ledger in range brings a card
screenshots.26-ledger-compare: The first address, to compare with the Ledger’s screen

title: Create or join a multisig account
description: Under Settings → Security → Multisig accounts, create an account from this phone, a Ledger and keys someone sent, or join one shared with you. Join an account also takes a SegWit v0 account, wsh(sortedmulti(…)), whose payments someone else builds. Signatures travel as PSBTs.
journey: Open Settings → Security → Multisig accounts and choose Create an account or Join an account.
Open the account and use Share with co-signers.

title: Join and co-sign a SegWit v0 multisig account
description: Join a SegWit v0 wsh(sortedmulti(…)) multisig account shared by co-signers, receive into it, review a co-signer’s PSBT, add this phone’s ECDSA signature, and watch the payment confirm.
journey: Open Settings → Security → Multisig accounts, join a SegWit v0 2-of-3 descriptor, and receive bitcoin into it.
Import a co-signer’s PSBT, review the payment, and add this phone’s ECDSA signature.
Finalize and broadcast the co-signed transaction and see it confirm.
limitations: SegWit v0 multisig accounts are join-only: another wallet builds the descriptor and PSBTs, and this phone reviews and co-signs.

screenshots.80-segwit-join: Joining a SegWit v0 2-of-3 multisig account
screenshots.81-segwit-funded: The SegWit v0 account receives bitcoin

title: Back up and restore
description: Automatic encrypted iCloud backup restores this phone’s signing key, history, multisig accounts, saved people and labels. Backup files remain available.
journey: Create a wallet; backup begins without an Enable step. A successful save appears only after iCloud acknowledges it.
On a replacement device, Winnow discovers backups automatically. Select one and authenticate; automatic updates resume using a separate record.
Settings → Backup has the iCloud backup switch, Save a backup file and Show recovery phrase. Without iCloud, keep a backup file that includes the recovery phrase for spending recovery.
limitations: Cloud and Keychain synchronization can be delayed. Other signers’ keys are not included. Older cloud copies may lack names and labels. Recovery words alone restore the wallet but not shared multisig accounts; those come back only from a backup file or the iCloud copy.

title: Accounts and paired Ledgers across devices
description: Multisig accounts and paired Ledgers backed up through iCloud follow your other devices automatically. A second device that does not hold the signing key lists the account under Watching with its balance and next address.
journey: Back up an account and paired Ledger from the first device.
Open Winnow on a second device signed into the same iCloud account and see the account listed under Watching.
Open the watch-only account page to inspect its balance and next address, and check the paired Ledger and multi-device sync status.
limitations: The recorded journey uses a simulated iCloud store shared between two device sessions rather than live Apple CloudKit.

title: Keep multiple profiles on one device
description: Under Settings → Profiles, keep more than one wallet profile on the same phone, rename them, and switch between them. Global sync keeps inactive profiles up to date in the background.
journey: Open Settings → Profiles, add a second profile on the same device, and rename both profiles.
Fund the inactive profile and confirm global sync discovers its balance in the background.
Sign a shared 2-of-2 payment with the first profile, switch directly to the second profile to add the second signature, and prepare to broadcast.

title: One home, and Settings for the rest
description: There is one mode. The home has the balance, Receive, Send, your multisig accounts, Activity and backup status. Settings holds Appearance, Network, Security, Backup and About. Send folds its fee controls under Fee.
journey: Create, receive, and send from the home.
Return to the home and see the balance and the payment in Activity.

title: Replace a pending payment with a higher fee
description: Review a replacement’s fee and change before authorizing it. The original remains visible as replaced.
journey: Open a pending outgoing payment from Activity and choose Bump fee.
Review the replacement’s fee and change before authorizing it. Activity keeps the original marked Replaced.

screenshots.51-fee-bump-confirmed: The replacement confirms; the original is marked Replaced

title: Inspect peers and control external disclosure
description: Inspect connected peers and network settings. Explorer links open only after an explicit warning about the information sent to that website.
journey: Open Settings → Network → Peers and routing to inspect connected peers.
Review the warning before opening an external explorer; cancel to stay in the app.
Use Reset and shuffle peers when you want to discard remembered candidates and reconnect.
When no peer can be reached, the home says Offline. The warning leads to Settings → Network → Sync, whose Retry reconnects.
limitations: Explorer websites are not wallet backends. A single or coordinated set of peers can still withhold information; multiple connections are not proof of independent operators.

screenshots.60-home-offline: No peers: the home says Offline

title: The peers each build ships
description: Each build ships the census peer list, checked against Winnow’s pinned signing key before it is bundled. The app downloads no census.
journey: Open Settings → Network → Peers and routing and read the shipped census’s observation date and candidate count.
Use Reset and shuffle peers to discard remembered candidates and reconnect.
limitations: The census is one trust source. Every peer still goes through the wallet’s normal checks. A new census arrives with a new build.
